arxiv-2101-06370.creator: Lili Du a,1 , Yongfu Wang b,2
arxiv-2101-06370.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Lili Du a,1 , Yongfu Wang b,2. In the classical survey (Chapter 16.2, Mathematics in industrial problem , Vol. 24, Springer-Verlag, New York, 1989), A. Friedman proposed an open problem on the collision of two incompressible jets emerging from two axially symmetric nozzles. In this paper, we concerned with the mathematical theory on this collision problem, and establish the well-posedness theory on hydrodynamic impinging outgoing jets issuing from two coaxial axially symmetric nozzles.

arxiv-2101-11671.title: Components of Eleven-dimensional Supergravity with Four Off-shell Supersymmetries
arxiv-2101-11671.creator: Katrin Becker, Daniel Butter, William D. Linch III, and Anindya Sengupta
arxiv-2101-11671.description: Abstract We derive the component structure of 11D, N = 1 / 8 N=1/8 supergravity linearized around eleven-dimensional Minkowski space. This theory represents 4 local supersymmetries closing onto 4 of the 11 spacetime translations without the use of equations of motion.

arxiv-2108-06555.title: Probing defect densities at the edges and inside Josephson junctions of superconducting qubits
arxiv-2108-06555.creator: Alexander Bilmes, Serhii Volosheniuk, Alexey V. Ustinov, Jürgen Lisenfeld
arxiv-2108-06555.description: Abstract Tunneling defects in disordered materials form spurious two-level systems which are a major source of decoherence for micro-fabricated quantum devices. For superconducting qubits, defects in tunnel barriers of submicrometer-sized Josephson junctions couple strongest to the qubit, which necessitates optimization of the junction fabrication to mitigate defect formation.

arxiv-2108-13113.title: BDD-Based Algorithm for SCC Decomposition of Edge-Coloured Graphs
arxiv-2108-13113.creator: Nikola Beneš, Luboš Brim, Samuel Pastva, David Šafránek
arxiv-2108-13113.description: Abstract . Edge-coloured directed graphs provide an essential structure for modelling and analysis of complex systems arising in many scientific disciplines (e.g. feature-oriented systems, gene regulatory networks, etc.). One of the fundamental problems for edge-coloured graphs is the detection of strongly connected components, or SCCs.

arxiv-2305-08613.title: Reconnection of infinitely thin antiparallel vortices and coherent structures
arxiv-2305-08613.creator: Sergei Iakunin, Luis Vega
arxiv-2305-08613.description: Abstract One of the characteristic features of turbulent flows is the emergence of many vortices which interact, deform, and intersect, generating a chaotic movement. The evolution of a pair of vortices, e.g. condensation trails of a plane, can be considered as a basic element of a turbulent flow.

arxiv-2305-14645.title: Iteratively Improving Biomedical Entity Linking and Event Extraction via Hard Expectation-Maximization
arxiv-2305-14645.creator: Xiaochu Li, Minqian Liu, Zhiyang Xu, Lifu HuangComputer Science DepartmentVirginia Tech {xiaocli, minqianliu, zhiyangx, lifuh}@vt.edu

arxiv-2311-03981.title: Non-singular word maps for linear groups
arxiv-2311-03981.creator: Henry Bradford, Jakob Schneider, Andreas Thom
arxiv-2311-03981.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Henry Bradford, Jakob Schneider, Andreas Thom. We study the word image of words with constants in GL ⁡ ( V ) \GL(V) and show that it is large provided the word satisfies some natural conditions on its length and its critical constants.

arxiv-2602-05601.title: Particle acceleration signatures in the time-dependent one-zone synchrotron self-Compton model of blazar flares
arxiv-2602-05601.creator: Paloma Thevenet, Andreas Zech, Catherine Boisson, Anton Dmytriiev
arxiv-2602-05601.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Paloma Thevenet, Andreas Zech, Catherine Boisson, Anton Dmytriiev. The study of multiwavelength flux and spectral variations during rapid flares from blazars provides strong constraints on the physical parameters of the compact emission regions responsible for these still poorly understood events.

pmc-11367120.title: Comparative effects of dietary muramidase and phytogenics on the growth performance and gastrointestinal functionality of broiler chickens
pmc-11367120.creator: Necmettin Ceylan, Cristiano Bortoluzzi, Oguz Gunturkun, Estefania Perez-Calvo
pmc-11367120.description: The objective of the present study was to compare the effectiveness of dietary supplementation of muramidase (MUR) and 2 phytogenic additives on the growth performance, intestinal morphology, bacteria load, and production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) of broiler chickens raised under field-like conditions.

pmc-11432567.title: Recent Insights into Roles of Hypoxia-Inducible Factors in Retinal Diseases
pmc-11432567.creator: Deokho Lee, Yohei Tomita, Yukihiro Miwa, Hiromitsu Kunimi, Ayaka Nakai, Chiho Shoda, Kazuno Negishi, Toshihide Kurihara, J Fielding Hejtmancik
pmc-11432567.description: Hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) are transcriptional factors that function as strong regulators of oxygen homeostasis and cellular metabolisms. The maintenance of cellular oxygen levels is critical as either insufficient or excessive oxygen affects development and physiologic and pathologic conditions. In the eye, retinas have a high metabolic demand for oxygen.

pmc-11618569.title: CMTM6 status predicts survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and correlates with PD-L1 expression
pmc-11618569.creator: Anne-Sophie Becker, Nicolas Wieder, Sarah Zonnur, Annette Zimpfer, Mareike Krause, Björn Schneider, Daniel Fabian Strüder, Ann-Sophie Burmeister, Andreas Erbersdobler, Christian Junghanss, Claudia Maletzki
pmc-11618569.description: We retrospectively analyzed 129 treatment-naïve head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCCs) for the expression of programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1), CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing 6 (CMTM6), tumor-infiltrating leukocytes (TILs), and tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). We evaluated the relationships among these markers, human papilloma virus (HPV) status, and overall survival (OS).

pmc-11703768.title: Enhancing Wear Resistance in Glass Ionomer Cement through Green-mediated Chitosan-, Titanium-, Zirconium-, and Hydroxyapatite-based Nanocomposites: An Analysis before and after Chewing Simulator Endurance
pmc-11703768.creator: Srinavasa Surya Sitaram, Jessy Paulraj, Subhabrata Maiti, Rajeshkumar Shanmugam
pmc-11703768.description: Aim and backgroundGlass ionomer cement (GIC) serves as a widely used restorative dental material, known for its direct bonding to tooth structures and fluoride-releasing properties. This study aims to investigate the enhancement of GIC through the incorporation of a green-mediated nanocomposite comprising chitosan, titanium, zirconium, and hydroxyapatite, with a focus on evaluating the wear resistance of the modified GIC.

pmc-12602330.title: Mutations of schizophrenia risk gene SETD1A dysregulate synaptic function in human neurons
pmc-12602330.creator: Xiao Su, Hanwen Zhang, Yan Hong, Qian Yang, Le Wang, Tiffany Le, Jiayi Liu, Lasya Cheruvu, Emily Labour, Siwei Zhang, Karla Mendez-Maldonado, Anat Kreimer, Hongjun Song, Guo-li Ming, Jubao Duan, Zhiping P. Pang
pmc-12602330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a complex neuropsychiatric disorder associated with both common risk variants of small effect sizes and rare risk variants of high penetrance. Rare premature open reading frame (ORF) termination variants in SETD1A (SET Domain Containing 1A) show a strong association with SCZ; however, it remains largely unclear how rare premature ORF termination variants in SETD1A contribute to the pathophysiology of SCZ.

pmc-12714495.title: Current Trends and Future Insights on Rosacea Treatment: A Bibliometric Analysis
pmc-12714495.creator: Dongxue Wang, Jinfang Zhang, Bin Wang, Jiefang Gao, Guoqiang Zhang
pmc-12714495.description: BackgroundRosacea involves immune, neurovascular, and microbial factors, but its complex mechanisms are poorly understood, hindering effective treatment development. This study aims to examine research trends and significant contributions in the treatment of rosacea.MethodsPublications related to rosacea treatment were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC).

pmc-12751676.title: Mapping the neural correlates of the effect of psycholinguistic variables on picture naming performance: a FDG-PET study across neurodegenerative diseases
pmc-12751676.creator: Francesca Conca, Valentina Esposito, Cristina Polito, Gaia C. Santi, Daniela M. Gibbons, Silvia P. Caminiti, Cecilia Boccalini, Carmen Morinelli, Valentina Berti, Salvatore Mazzeo, Valentina Bessi, Alessandra Marcone, Sandro Iannaccone, Sandro Sorbi, Daniela Perani, Stefano F. Cappa, Eleonora Catric
pmc-12751676.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPicture naming performance is influenced by the properties of the stimuli and of the words to be retrieved, such as word length and lexical frequency. Significant inconsistencies, however, remain regarding the brain regions mediating these effects in neurodegenerative patients.

pmc-13530744.creator: Cameron Bussey-Sutton, Kobe Rodney, Vishal Sundaram, Alexander J. Egol, Laith Jazrawi, Kirk A. Campbell, Eric J. Strauss, Heath P. Gould

pmc-13611119.title: Multi-Response Optimization of FDM Process Parameters for Enhanced Mechanical Performance and Reduced Weight of PLA and PLA-CF 3D-Printed Parts
pmc-13611119.creator: Mustafa Saleh
pmc-13611119.description: This work investigates the influence of fused deposition modeling (FDM) parameters on the tensile properties and material consumption of FDM-printed samples. The study focused on extrusion-related parameters that directly govern material deposition during FDM printing, including extrusion temperature (ET), layer thickness (LT), and extrusion multiplier (EM).

pmc-13672765.title: The added value of post-mortem MRI in forensic imaging: an observational study in the Netherlands
pmc-13672765.creator: Cédrique A. S. Gregoire, Maartje M. A. Eggen, Geneviève A. J. C. Crombag, Alida A. Postma, J. Martijn Nobel
pmc-13672765.description: ObjectivesIn the Netherlands, post-mortem radiology aids forensic investigation, using a full-body post-mortem computed tomography (PMCT) scan and a post-mortem magnetic resonance imaging (PMMRI) scan in specific cases. Application of PMMRI varies between countries and institutions in the absence of international guidelines. This study analyses current use and added value of PMMRI in a single forensic imaging institution in the Netherlands.
